# A Field Study of Seed Dispersal
# version: Camera-ready, ICMLX 2023
entity,mean_annual_runoff

K-17,1647.5
N-26,1140.8

sections: Abstract

We report mean annual runoff measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2021 and 2023. A pilot survey in 2018 had put the regional mean annual runoff at 1005.4 mm; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of seed dispersal relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2020 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2023 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the mean annual runoff for each station in the 2023 campaign. The largest change relative to 2020 was observed at station N-26.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Abernathy et al. (2017). [2] Wenzel and Mattheus (2019). [3] Zelenko et al. (2020).

tables.caption: Table 3: Mean annual runoff in the 2020 campaign
